swms.title: Working with Hazardous Substances
swms.workActivity: Use, handling, storage, and disposal of hazardous substances on construction sites including paints, solvents, adhesives, sealants, waterproofing membranes, concrete admixtures, herbicides, pesticides, cleaning agents, fuels, and other chemical products used in construction and maintenance activities.
swms.hazards: Skin and eye contact with corrosive, irritant, or sensitising chemicals; inhalation of vapours, fumes, mists, and dusts from hazardous substances; ingestion through contaminated hands or food; fire and explosion from flammable and combustible liquids; chemical reactions from incompatible substances stored or mixed together; spills and leaks causing environmental contamination; inadequate ventilation in enclosed work areas.
swms.risks: Chemical burns to skin and eyes; respiratory illness, occupational asthma, or chemical sensitisation from inhalation; poisoning from ingestion; fire or explosion from flammable substances; environmental contamination from spills; long-term health effects from chronic exposure to carcinogens or sensitisers.
swms.controls: Obtain and read the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) for every hazardous substance before use — SDS must be accessible on site at all times. Apply the hierarchy of controls: eliminate the hazardous substance where possible; substitute with a less hazardous product; use engineering controls (LEV, ventilation); use administrative controls (safe work procedures, exposure limits); use PPE as the last line of defence. Never mix chemicals unless the SDS or manufacturer explicitly states it is safe to do so. Store flammable liquids in a bunded, ventilated flammables cabinet away from ignition sources. Ensure adequate ventilation in all work areas — use forced ventilation fans in enclosed spaces. Implement a no eating, drinking, or smoking rule in all chemical work areas. Wash hands thoroughly before eating, drinking, or using the toilet. Dispose of chemical waste in accordance with the SDS and local regulations.
swms.ppe: Chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile, neoprene, or PVC as specified by SDS); Safety glasses or chemical splash goggles; Face shield for splash risk; Respiratory protection as specified by SDS (P2 for dusts and mists; organic vapour cartridge for solvent vapours; supplied air for high-concentration or confined space use); Chemical-resistant apron or coveralls; Safety boots with chemical-resistant uppers.
swms.plantEquipment: Bunded flammables storage cabinet; Spill kit (absorbent material, bunding, disposal bags); Eyewash station; Forced ventilation fans; SDS register and folder; Chemical-resistant containers and dispensing equipment; Waste disposal containers (labelled).
swms.trainingCompetency: All workers to receive hazardous substances awareness training before handling chemicals. Chemical applicators (herbicides, pesticides) to hold a current ChemCert or equivalent licence. Workers using respiratory protection to be fit-tested and trained in correct donning and doffing. Supervisor to maintain a site chemical register and ensure current SDS are available for all products on site.
swms.emergencyControls: Eyewash station positioned within 10 seconds travel of all chemical work areas — test weekly. Spill kit on site and workers trained in its use. In the event of a significant chemical spill — stop work, evacuate the area, contain the spill using the spill kit, call 000 if the substance is toxic or flammable and the spill cannot be safely contained. Chemical splash to eyes — flush with clean water for 15 minutes, call 000. Inhalation of fumes — move to fresh air, call 000 if symptoms persist. Have SDS available for emergency services.
swms.environmentalControls: Never pour chemical waste down drains, into waterways, or onto the ground. Dispose of chemical waste at an approved facility — retain disposal records. Contain all spills immediately using the spill kit. Store chemicals in bunded areas to prevent spill runoff. Return unused chemicals to the supplier where possible.
swms.signOffRequirements: Chemical register and SDS folder on site before any hazardous substances are brought to site. Spill kit and eyewash station in place before work commences. Workers to sign SWMS before handling hazardous substances. Supervisor sign-off each day.

swms.title: Using Power Tools
swms.workActivity: Use of electric, battery, and pneumatic power tools on construction sites including angle grinders, circular saws, jigsaws, reciprocating saws, drills, hammer drills, routers, nail guns, impact drivers, planers, and sanders for cutting, drilling, grinding, fastening, and finishing tasks.
swms.hazards: Contact with rotating blades, discs, and drill bits causing lacerations and amputations; projectile ejection of blade fragments, disc fragments, workpiece material, and fasteners; electric shock from damaged power tools or leads; hand-arm vibration from prolonged use of vibrating tools; noise from power tools; dust inhalation (silica, wood dust, MDF dust) from cutting and grinding; fire from sparks near flammable materials; entanglement of clothing or hair in rotating parts; nail gun penetrating injuries; working near others.
swms.risks: Severe lacerations and amputations from blade and disc contact; eye injury from projectiles; electrocution; hand-arm vibration syndrome (HAVS) from prolonged use; hearing damage; respiratory illness from dust; fire; penetrating nail gun injury.
swms.controls: Inspect every power tool before use — remove from service any tool with a damaged guard, frayed lead, cracked housing, or defective safety mechanism; tag out and report to supervisor. Never remove or bypass guards — all guards must be in place and functioning before use. Wear appropriate PPE for the tool and task — safety glasses minimum; face shield for grinding; hearing protection for all power tool use; P2 respirator for dust-generating tasks. Secure the workpiece with clamps or a vice — never hold the workpiece by hand when cutting or drilling. Disconnect from power before changing blades, discs, or bits. Angle grinder — use only discs rated for the grinder's RPM; inspect disc for cracks before fitting; never use a cutting disc for grinding or vice versa; stand to the side of the disc plane when starting. Nail gun — sequential trip mode only; never bypass the safety tip; keep finger off trigger when carrying; never point at another person. Implement a tool rotation plan to limit continuous vibrating tool use to 30 minutes per operator. Establish an exclusion zone around power tool operations — no bystanders within the projectile hazard zone.
swms.ppe: Safety glasses (minimum) — face shield for angle grinding and masonry cutting; Hearing protection for all power tool use; P2 respirator for dust-generating tasks (cutting, grinding, sanding); Cut-resistant gloves (Level C) for blade-adjacent tasks — note: do not wear gloves when operating drill presses or lathes (entanglement risk); Safety boots with steel cap and midsole; Close-fitting clothing — no loose sleeves, ties, or jewellery near rotating parts.
swms.plantEquipment: Angle grinders; Circular saws; Jigsaws; Reciprocating saws; Drills and hammer drills; Routers; Nail guns (framing, finish, brad); Sanders; Planers; RCD (residual current device) for all corded electric tools; Extension leads (heavy duty, rated for tool load); Clamps and vices; On-tool dust extraction.
swms.trainingCompetency: All workers to receive power tool safety training before use. Nail gun operators to complete nail gun safety training. Angle grinder operators to be competent in disc selection, fitting, and safe use. Supervisor to maintain a tool register and ensure all tools are inspected and tagged. All workers to hold a current White Card.
swms.emergencyControls: First aid kit on site with wound dressings for lacerations. In the event of a severe laceration — apply direct pressure, call 000 immediately; do not remove embedded objects. Nail gun penetrating injury — do not remove nail, immobilise the affected area, call 000. Eye injury from projectile — do not rub, cover the eye, call 000. Electric shock — do not touch the casualty if still in contact with the power source; isolate power, call 000. Emergency contacts posted on site.
swms.environmentalControls: Collect all sawdust, swarf, and grinding dust — dispose of as construction waste. Prevent dust and debris from entering stormwater drains. Dispose of damaged or worn blades and discs in a puncture-resistant container.
swms.signOffRequirements: Pre-use tool inspection completed and recorded before each shift. Damaged tools tagged out and removed from service. Workers to sign SWMS before commencing. Supervisor sign-off each day.

swms.title: Balustrade and Handrail Installation
swms.workActivity: Installation of balustrades and handrails including glass, stainless steel, aluminium, and timber systems on stairs, decks, balconies, and mezzanine floors. Includes cutting, drilling, grinding, fixing posts and top rails, setting glass panels, and applying sealants and fixings.
swms.hazards: Working at heights on stairs, balconies, and mezzanine edges without edge protection during installation; handling and cutting glass panels (sharp edges, breakage); manual handling of heavy posts, rails, and glass panels; use of angle grinders and power drills (sparks, noise, vibration); chemical exposure from sealants, adhesives, and glass setting compounds; falls through unprotected openings; struck by dropped tools or materials from height.
swms.risks: Fatal or serious injury from falls through unprotected edges or openings; severe lacerations from broken or cut glass; musculoskeletal injuries from manual handling; eye injury from grinding sparks or glass fragments; chemical burns or sensitisation from sealants; hearing damage from power tools.
swms.controls: Install temporary edge protection (barriers, safety mesh, or scaffolding) at all open edges and stair voids before commencing installation — do not remove until permanent balustrade is certified as compliant and load-tested. Handle glass panels with suction cups and a minimum two-person lift; wear cut-resistant gloves at all times when handling glass. Inspect all glass panels for chips or cracks before installation — do not install damaged panels. Use angle grinder guards and face shield when cutting or grinding metal. Ensure all post fixings are drilled and anchored per engineer specifications — do not substitute fixing types without approval. Apply sealants in ventilated areas; wear nitrile gloves and safety glasses. Confirm structural adequacy of substrate (deck, slab, stair stringer) before fixing posts — obtain engineer sign-off for non-standard substrates.
swms.ppe: Hard hat; Safety harness with lanyard when working within 2m of an unprotected edge; Cut-resistant gloves (Level C minimum) for glass handling; Safety glasses and face shield when grinding or cutting; Safety boots with steel cap and midsole; Hearing protection when using angle grinders or hammer drills; Nitrile gloves when applying sealants.
swms.plantEquipment: Angle grinder with cutting and grinding discs; Hammer drill and core drill; Glass suction cups (rated for panel weight); Torque wrench; Silicone gun; Spirit level and laser level; Scaffolding or edge protection barriers; Temporary handrail clamps.
swms.trainingCompetency: Workers must hold a current White Card. Working at heights training and harness use required for all elevated work. Glass handling training required for glazed balustrade systems. Balustrade installations must comply with AS 1657 and NCC requirements — supervisor to confirm compliance before handover.
swms.emergencyControls: First aid kit on site with wound dressings for lacerations. In the event of glass breakage causing injury — apply direct pressure, call 000 for serious lacerations. Do not attempt to remove embedded glass. Rescue plan for suspended worker. Emergency contacts posted on site.
swms.environmentalControls: Collect all glass offcuts and metal swarf — dispose of in designated waste containers. Do not allow glass fragments to enter stormwater drains. Contain sealant waste and dispose of correctly.
swms.signOffRequirements: Temporary edge protection inspection before work commences. Engineer sign-off on post fixing specification. Load test and compliance check on completion. Workers to sign SWMS before commencing. Supervisor sign-off.

swms.title: Bricklaying
swms.workActivity: Bricklaying and blockwork construction including setting out, mortar mixing, laying bricks and blocks, building piers, walls, and retaining walls, installing lintels, and pointing and cleaning finished work. Includes work at ground level and at heights using scaffolding.
swms.hazards: Manual handling of heavy bricks, blocks, and mortar (repetitive and heavy loads); working at heights on scaffolding; mortar and cement burns (alkaline burns to skin and eyes); silica dust from cutting bricks and blocks with angle grinder or masonry saw; noise from masonry cutting; falling bricks or materials from scaffold; scaffold instability; UV radiation and heat stress.
swms.risks: Musculoskeletal injuries from repetitive heavy manual handling; falls from scaffold; chemical burns from wet mortar and cement; silicosis from silica dust inhalation; hearing damage; struck by falling materials; heat exhaustion.
swms.controls: Use mechanical aids (brick trolley, forklift, hoist) to deliver materials to scaffold level — do not hand-carry full packs up scaffold. Implement a manual handling rotation plan — limit continuous bricklaying to 45 minutes before a break. Wear waterproof gloves and wash skin immediately if mortar contact occurs. Wet-cut all bricks and blocks where practicable — if dry cutting is unavoidable, use on-tool dust extraction and wear a P2 respirator. Scaffold to be erected by a licensed scaffolder and inspected before each shift — ensure toe boards, mid-rails, and top rails are in place. Establish exclusion zone below scaffold during material loading. Hearing protection mandatory when operating masonry saw. Implement heat management plan for summer work.
swms.ppe: Hard hat; High visibility vest; Safety boots with steel cap; Waterproof gloves for mortar work; Safety glasses; P2 respirator when cutting masonry (minimum — P3 for high-silica content materials); Hearing protection when using masonry saw or angle grinder; Knee pads for ground-level work; Sunscreen SPF50+ and sun-protective clothing.
swms.plantEquipment: Masonry saw (wet); Angle grinder with diamond blade; Brick trolley; Scaffold and hoist; Mortar mixer; Spirit level and laser level; Trowels, jointers, and hand tools; Lintel lifting equipment.
swms.trainingCompetency: Bricklayers to hold Certificate III in Bricklaying/Blocklaying or demonstrated trade competency. Scaffold erectors must hold a scaffolding licence. All workers must hold a current White Card. Silica dust awareness training required.
swms.emergencyControls: Eyewash station near mortar mixing area. First aid kit with burn treatment supplies on site. In the event of scaffold collapse — evacuate area, call 000, do not re-enter. Mortar burn to eyes — flush with clean water for 15 minutes, seek medical attention.
swms.environmentalControls: Mortar and cement washout to designated bunded washout area — not to stormwater drains. Collect brick offcuts and dispose of as construction waste. Dust suppression by wet cutting and water application. Protect adjacent surfaces from mortar spatter.
swms.signOffRequirements: Scaffold inspection certificate before elevated work commences. Workers to sign SWMS before commencing. Supervisor sign-off each day.

swms.title: Building Inspection
swms.workActivity: Building inspection activities including pre-purchase inspections, progress inspections, final inspections, and defect inspections on residential and commercial buildings. Includes accessing roof spaces, subfloor areas, roof exteriors, and all areas of a building under construction or occupation.
swms.hazards: Falls from roof and elevated areas; falls through fragile roof surfaces (skylights, fibro, corroded sheeting); confined space hazards in subfloor and roof spaces (restricted access, low oxygen, vermin); electrical hazards from exposed wiring; asbestos in pre-1990 buildings; manual handling when accessing tight spaces; slips and trips on uneven or cluttered surfaces; working alone.
swms.risks: Fatal or serious injury from falls; asphyxiation or toxic exposure in confined spaces; electrocution from exposed wiring; asbestos-related disease; musculoskeletal injuries; slips and falls.
swms.controls: Do not walk on fragile roof surfaces — use roof ladder or crawl board; assess roof condition before accessing. Do not enter subfloor or roof spaces with restricted access without confirming ventilation is adequate — use atmospheric monitor if enclosed. Identify and avoid all exposed or damaged electrical wiring — do not touch; report to client. Assume all materials in pre-1990 buildings may contain asbestos — do not disturb; note in report and recommend testing. Implement a lone worker check-in procedure — notify a contact before entering roof or subfloor spaces and check in on exit. Wear appropriate PPE for each area accessed. Do not enter any area assessed as structurally unsafe.
swms.ppe: Hard hat for roof and construction site access; Safety boots with non-slip soles; Safety glasses; P2 respirator for roof spaces and subfloor areas (dust, insulation fibres, potential asbestos); Disposable coveralls for subfloor and roof space access; Gloves; Torch and head lamp; Knee pads for subfloor access.
swms.plantEquipment: Roof ladder and crawl board; Atmospheric gas monitor (for enclosed subfloor/roof spaces); Torch and head lamp; Moisture meter; Thermal imaging camera; Inspection mirror; Camera.
swms.trainingCompetency: Building inspector to hold a relevant licence or registration (e.g. Queensland Building and Construction Commission licence). Asbestos awareness training required. Working at heights training for roof access. Lone worker safety procedure training.
swms.emergencyControls: Lone worker check-in procedure in place before entering confined or elevated areas. First aid kit in vehicle. If inspector becomes unwell in a confined space — exit immediately, call 000. Emergency contacts confirmed before commencing each inspection.
swms.environmentalControls: Do not disturb suspected asbestos or hazardous materials during inspection. Decontaminate boots and coveralls before leaving site if asbestos or contamination is suspected.
swms.signOffRequirements: Lone worker check-in confirmed before commencing. Inspector to sign SWMS before each inspection. Inspection report to document all identified hazards.

swms.title: Cabinet and Joinery Installation
swms.workActivity: Installation of kitchen, bathroom, laundry, and built-in cabinets and joinery including unpacking and handling cabinet carcasses, fixing wall and base cabinets, installing benchtops (stone, laminate, timber), fitting doors, drawers, and hardware, and making plumbing and electrical penetrations.
swms.hazards: Manual handling of heavy cabinet carcasses, stone benchtops, and appliances; use of power tools (drills, jigsaws, routers, circular saws); silica dust from cutting engineered stone benchtops; lacerations from sharp edges of cabinets, sheet material, and stone; working at heights on step ladders for overhead cabinets; electrical hazards from working near existing circuits; chemical exposure from adhesives and sealants.
swms.risks: Musculoskeletal injuries from manual handling of heavy benchtops and carcasses; silicosis from engineered stone dust; lacerations from sharp edges and power tools; falls from step ladders; electrocution from undiscovered live circuits; eye injury from dust and debris.
swms.controls: Stone benchtop handling — minimum two-person lift; use mechanical lifting aids (suction cups, panel carrier) for slabs >30kg; never lift a stone benchtop alone. Engineered stone cutting — wet cut only using on-tool water suppression; wear a P2 respirator minimum; if dry cutting is unavoidable, use LEV and P3 respirator — note that dry cutting of engineered stone is prohibited under WHS regulations in most jurisdictions. Confirm all electrical circuits in the work area are isolated before drilling or cutting into walls. Use push sticks and guards on all power saws. Wear cut-resistant gloves when handling sheet material and stone edges. Step ladders — ensure all four feet are on a stable, level surface; do not overreach.
swms.ppe: Safety boots with steel cap; Safety glasses; Cut-resistant gloves (Level C) for stone and sheet material handling; P2 respirator for all stone cutting (P3 for engineered stone); Hearing protection when using power saws; Knee pads for floor-level installation work.
swms.plantEquipment: Circular saw; Jigsaw; Router; Drill/driver; Stone suction cups and panel carrier; Spirit level and laser level; Silicone gun; Clamps; Step ladder.
swms.trainingCompetency: Cabinet makers and installers to hold Certificate III in Cabinet Making or demonstrated trade competency. Engineered stone silica dust training mandatory — workers must be aware of the prohibition on dry cutting. All workers to hold a current White Card.
swms.emergencyControls: First aid kit on site. In the event of a laceration from stone or sheet material — apply direct pressure, call 000 for serious wounds. Silica dust exposure — move to fresh air, seek medical attention if respiratory symptoms develop. Emergency contacts confirmed before commencing.
swms.environmentalControls: Collect all stone and timber offcuts for disposal as construction waste. Wet cutting slurry to be contained and disposed of — not to stormwater. Adhesive and sealant waste disposed of correctly.
swms.signOffRequirements: Electrical isolation confirmed before wall penetrations. Workers to sign SWMS before commencing. Supervisor sign-off on completion.

swms.title: Carpenter — Cladding
swms.workActivity: Installation of external wall cladding systems including fibre cement, timber weatherboard, compressed sheet, and composite cladding products. Includes setting out, cutting, fixing, and finishing cladding, installation of flashings, trims, and sealants, and working from scaffolding or EWP.
swms.hazards: Working at heights on scaffolding or EWP; silica dust from cutting fibre cement cladding; manual handling of long and heavy cladding sheets; lacerations from sharp sheet edges; noise from power saws and nail guns; UV radiation and heat stress; chemical exposure from sealants and primers; nail gun injuries.
swms.risks: Falls from scaffold or EWP; silicosis from fibre cement dust; musculoskeletal injuries; lacerations; hearing damage; heat exhaustion; penetrating nail gun injury.
swms.controls: Scaffold to be erected by a licensed scaffolder and inspected before each shift — full edge protection required. Fibre cement cutting — wet cut or use on-tool dust extraction; wear P2 respirator minimum; never dry cut fibre cement without LEV. Use panel carrier or two-person lift for sheets >20kg. Wear cut-resistant gloves when handling sheet edges. Nail gun — never bypass safety mechanism; keep finger off trigger when not nailing; never point at another person; use sequential trip mode. Hearing protection mandatory when using power saws and nail guns. Implement heat management plan for summer work.
swms.ppe: Hard hat; High visibility vest; Safety boots with steel cap; Safety harness when working on EWP or unprotected edges; P2 respirator for fibre cement cutting; Cut-resistant gloves; Safety glasses; Hearing protection when using power saws or nail guns; Sunscreen SPF50+.
swms.plantEquipment: Circular saw with dust extraction; Fibre cement shears; Nail gun (first-fix framing nailer or clout nailer); Scaffolding or EWP; Panel carrier; Spirit level and chalk line; Silicone gun.
swms.trainingCompetency: Carpenters to hold Certificate III in Carpentry or demonstrated trade competency. Scaffold erectors must hold a scaffolding licence. EWP operators must hold a relevant high risk work licence (WP class). Silica dust awareness training required. All workers to hold a current White Card.
swms.emergencyControls: First aid kit on site. Nail gun penetration injury — do not remove nail, immobilise, call 000. Scaffold collapse — evacuate, call 000, do not re-enter. Emergency contacts posted on site.
swms.environmentalControls: Collect all fibre cement offcuts and dispose of as construction waste — do not break up or grind on site without dust controls. Wet cutting slurry contained and disposed of correctly. Sealant waste disposed of correctly.
swms.signOffRequirements: Scaffold inspection certificate before elevated work. Workers to sign SWMS before commencing. Supervisor sign-off each day.

swms.title: Carpenter — Second Fix (Fixing)
swms.workActivity: Second fix carpentry including installation of internal doors and door frames, skirting boards, architraves, window stools and reveals, built-in wardrobes, shelving, stair balustrades, and all internal timber joinery and hardware. Includes use of nail guns, routers, jigsaws, and hand tools.
swms.hazards: Nail gun injuries (penetrating injury from misfires or ricochets); lacerations from power saws, chisels, and sharp timber edges; manual handling of door frames, doors, and large timber components; dust from sanding and cutting MDF and timber (silica, wood dust); noise from nail guns and power tools; working on step ladders for high-level fixing; chemical exposure from adhesives and finishes.
swms.risks: Penetrating nail gun injury; lacerations; musculoskeletal injuries; respiratory illness from wood dust and MDF dust; hearing damage; falls from step ladders; eye injury from dust and debris.
swms.controls: Nail gun — use sequential trip mode only (not bump fire); never bypass safety tip; keep finger off trigger when carrying; never point at another person; inspect nail gun before use and remove from service if safety tip is damaged. MDF cutting — use on-tool dust extraction; wear P2 respirator; MDF dust is a known respiratory hazard. Wear cut-resistant gloves when handling rough-sawn timber and sheet edges. Step ladders — four feet on stable, level surface; do not overreach; face the ladder when climbing. Hearing protection mandatory when using nail guns and power saws. Ensure adequate ventilation when using adhesives and finishes.
swms.ppe: Safety boots with steel cap; Safety glasses; Cut-resistant gloves for timber handling; P2 respirator for MDF and timber dust; Hearing protection when using nail guns and power saws; Knee pads for floor-level work.
swms.plantEquipment: Finish nailer and brad nailer; Circular saw; Jigsaw; Router; Mitre saw; Drill/driver; Chisels and hand tools; Step ladder; Dust extraction unit.
swms.trainingCompetency: Carpenters to hold Certificate III in Carpentry or demonstrated trade competency. Nail gun training required before use. All workers to hold a current White Card.
swms.emergencyControls: First aid kit on site. Nail gun penetrating injury — do not remove nail, immobilise the affected limb, call 000 immediately. Eye injury from debris — do not rub, flush with clean water, seek medical attention. Emergency contacts confirmed before commencing.
swms.environmentalControls: Collect all timber and MDF offcuts for disposal as construction waste. Dust extraction waste disposed of correctly. Adhesive and finish waste disposed of correctly.
swms.signOffRequirements: Workers to sign SWMS before commencing. Supervisor sign-off on completion of each room or area.

swms.title: Carpenter — Framing
swms.workActivity: Structural timber framing of residential and commercial buildings including wall frames, floor frames, roof trusses, and rafters. Includes setting out, cutting, nailing, and erecting wall frames, installing top and bottom plates, noggins, lintels, and trimmers, and erecting roof trusses by crane or manually.
swms.hazards: Working at heights during wall frame erection and roof framing; falls through floor openings and stair voids; falling timber members during erection; manual handling of heavy timber members and wall frames; nail gun injuries; noise from nail guns and power saws; silica dust from cutting engineered timber products (LVL, I-joists); crane and rigging hazards during truss erection; UV radiation and heat stress.
swms.risks: Fatal or serious injury from falls; crush injuries from falling timber members; penetrating nail gun injury; musculoskeletal injuries; hearing damage; respiratory illness from engineered timber dust; crane-related injuries.
swms.controls: Install temporary edge protection and floor void covers before commencing elevated framing work — maintain throughout. Erect wall frames using a crane or wall frame jack — do not manually push up frames without adequate crew and a brace plan. Brace all wall frames immediately on erection before releasing crane or moving on. Roof truss erection — use a crane with a dogman; establish exclusion zone under lift; workers on top plate to wear harness anchored to certified anchor points. Nail gun — sequential trip mode only; inspect before use. Engineered timber cutting — use on-tool dust extraction; wear P2 respirator. Hearing protection mandatory when using nail guns and power saws. Implement heat management plan for summer roof framing.
swms.ppe: Hard hat; High visibility vest; Safety boots with steel cap; Safety harness with double lanyard for roof framing and truss erection; Cut-resistant gloves; Safety glasses; P2 respirator for engineered timber cutting; Hearing protection when using nail guns and power saws; Sunscreen SPF50+.
swms.plantEquipment: Framing nail gun; Circular saw; Mitre saw; Reciprocating saw; Crane (for truss erection); Wall frame jack; Temporary bracing; Floor void covers; Scaffolding or edge protection; Spirit level and chalk line.
swms.trainingCompetency: Carpenters to hold Certificate III in Carpentry or demonstrated trade competency. Crane operator must hold a relevant high risk work licence; dogman must hold a dogging licence. Working at heights training and harness use required. All workers to hold a current White Card.
swms.emergencyControls: First aid kit on site. In the event of a falling timber member — evacuate exclusion zone, call 000 for injury. Nail gun penetrating injury — do not remove nail, call 000. Rescue plan for suspended worker. Emergency contacts posted on site.
swms.environmentalControls: Collect all timber offcuts for disposal or recycling. Protect stormwater drains from sawdust and timber waste. Engineered timber offcuts to be disposed of as construction waste.
swms.signOffRequirements: Temporary edge protection and void covers in place before elevated work. Crane lift plan signed off before truss erection. Workers to sign SWMS before commencing. Supervisor sign-off each day.

swms.title: Carpenter — Lockup
swms.workActivity: Lockup stage carpentry including installation of external doors and door frames, windows and window frames, external trims, fascias, bargeboards, eaves lining, and weatherproofing elements. Includes working from scaffolding and ladders on the building exterior.
swms.hazards: Working at heights on scaffolding and ladders; manual handling of heavy door and window frames and glass units; lacerations from glass and sharp aluminium or timber frame edges; nail gun injuries; noise from nail guns and power saws; UV radiation and heat stress; chemical exposure from sealants and flashings tape; working near overhead power lines.
swms.risks: Falls from scaffold or ladder; musculoskeletal injuries from manual handling; lacerations from glass and frame edges; penetrating nail gun injury; hearing damage; heat exhaustion; electrocution from power lines.
swms.controls: Scaffold to be erected by a licensed scaffolder and inspected before each shift — full edge protection required. Ladders — inspect before use; secure top and base; maintain three points of contact; do not overreach. Window and door units — two-person minimum lift for units >20kg; use suction cups for glass units. Wear cut-resistant gloves when handling aluminium frames and glass. Identify and maintain minimum 3m exclusion zone from overhead power lines before commencing external work. Nail gun — sequential trip mode only; inspect before use. Sealants — apply in ventilated conditions; wear nitrile gloves and safety glasses. Implement heat management plan for summer work.
swms.ppe: Hard hat; High visibility vest; Safety boots with steel cap; Safety harness when working on EWP or unprotected edges; Cut-resistant gloves; Safety glasses; Hearing protection when using nail guns and power saws; Nitrile gloves for sealant application; Sunscreen SPF50+.
swms.plantEquipment: Framing nail gun; Circular saw; Drill/driver; Scaffolding; Extension ladder; Glass suction cups; Silicone gun; Spirit level and laser level.
swms.trainingCompetency: Carpenters to hold Certificate III in Carpentry or demonstrated trade competency. Scaffold erectors must hold a scaffolding licence. Working at heights training required. All workers to hold a current White Card.
swms.emergencyControls: First aid kit on site. Laceration from glass — apply direct pressure, call 000 for serious wounds; do not remove embedded glass. Nail gun penetrating injury — do not remove nail, call 000. Emergency contacts posted on site.
swms.environmentalControls: Collect all timber and aluminium offcuts for disposal. Sealant waste disposed of correctly. Protect stormwater drains from sawdust and construction debris.
swms.signOffRequirements: Scaffold inspection certificate before elevated work. Workers to sign SWMS before commencing. Supervisor sign-off each day.

swms.title: Ceramic and Stone Tiling
swms.workActivity: Installation of ceramic, porcelain, and natural stone tiles on floors, walls, and wet areas including surface preparation, waterproofing membrane application, adhesive mixing and application, tile cutting, grouting, and sealing. Includes wall and floor tiling in bathrooms, kitchens, laundries, and external areas.
swms.hazards: Silica dust from cutting ceramic, porcelain, and natural stone tiles (angle grinder or tile saw); manual handling of heavy tile boxes and stone slabs; chemical exposure from waterproofing membranes, tile adhesives, and grout (skin and eye irritation, sensitisation); prolonged kneeling and awkward postures; noise from tile saw and angle grinder; lacerations from sharp tile edges and broken tiles; working in wet areas (slippery surfaces).
swms.risks: Silicosis from silica dust inhalation; musculoskeletal injuries from manual handling and prolonged kneeling; chemical burns or sensitisation from adhesives and waterproofing products; lacerations from sharp tile edges; hearing damage; slips and falls on wet surfaces.
swms.controls: Tile cutting — wet cut using tile saw with water suppression at all times; if angle grinder cutting is required, use on-tool water attachment or LEV and wear P2 respirator minimum — note that dry cutting of porcelain and stone is a high silica dust risk. Wear cut-resistant gloves when handling cut tiles and broken tile pieces. Read SDS for all adhesives, waterproofing membranes, and grout products before use — wear nitrile gloves and safety glasses; ensure adequate ventilation. Manual handling — use tile trolley for heavy boxes; team lift for large-format stone tiles >25kg. Implement a kneeling rotation plan — use knee pads and change posture regularly. Hearing protection mandatory when using tile saw and angle grinder. Keep wet area floors dry and clear of tile offcuts to prevent slips.
swms.ppe: Safety boots with non-slip soles; Safety glasses; P2 respirator for all tile cutting; Cut-resistant gloves (Level C) for tile handling; Nitrile gloves for adhesive and waterproofing application; Hearing protection when using tile saw or angle grinder; Knee pads.
swms.plantEquipment: Wet tile saw; Angle grinder with diamond blade and water attachment; Tile nipper; Notched trowels; Grout float; Rubber mallet; Tile spacers; Mixing drill and bucket; Tile trolley; Waterproofing roller and brush.
swms.trainingCompetency: Tilers to hold Certificate III in Wall and Floor Tiling or demonstrated trade competency. Silica dust awareness training mandatory. Waterproofing application — tiler to hold a waterproofing licence or competency where required by jurisdiction. All workers to hold a current White Card.
swms.emergencyControls: First aid kit on site with wound dressings for lacerations. Eyewash station near adhesive and waterproofing mixing area. Chemical splash to eyes — flush with clean water for 15 minutes, seek medical attention, have SDS available. Laceration from tile — apply direct pressure, seek medical attention for deep wounds.
swms.environmentalControls: Tile cutting slurry to be contained and disposed of — not to stormwater drains. Collect all tile offcuts and dispose of as construction waste. Adhesive and grout waste disposed of correctly. Protect adjacent surfaces from adhesive and grout spatter.
swms.signOffRequirements: Waterproofing inspection and sign-off before tiling commences in wet areas. Workers to sign SWMS before commencing. Supervisor sign-off on completion of waterproofing and on final tiling.

swms.title: General Site Safety — High Risk Construction Work
swms.workActivity: General construction site activities including site establishment, material handling, and general labour tasks on a high risk construction site.
swms.hazards: Uneven ground and trip hazards; falling objects from overhead work; moving plant and machinery; manual handling injuries; electrical hazards from temporary power; dust and noise exposure; UV radiation; heat stress.
swms.risks: Slips, trips and falls; struck by falling objects; crush injuries from plant; musculoskeletal injuries; electrocution; respiratory illness; hearing damage; heat exhaustion.
swms.controls: Conduct daily site inspection before work commences. Ensure all workers have current site induction. Maintain clear pedestrian pathways separated from plant movement zones. Erect exclusion zones under overhead work. All electrical equipment to be tested and tagged. Provide and enforce use of appropriate PPE. Implement heat management plan in hot weather. Conduct regular toolbox talks.
swms.ppe: Hard hat (AS/NZS 1801); High visibility vest (Class D/N); Safety boots with steel cap (AS/NZS 2210.3); Safety glasses (AS/NZS 1337); Hearing protection where noise >85dB; Sunscreen SPF50+ and sun-protective clothing; Gloves for manual handling tasks.
swms.plantEquipment: Excavators, skid steers, forklifts, elevated work platforms, concrete pumps, generators, power tools, hand tools.
swms.trainingCompetency: All workers must hold a current General Construction Induction (White Card). Plant operators must hold relevant high risk work licences. First aid officer on site at all times. Emergency warden designated.
swms.emergencyControls: Emergency assembly point clearly marked at site entry. First aid kit location communicated at induction. Nearest hospital: confirm at site establishment. Emergency contacts posted in site office. Incident reporting procedure communicated to all workers.
swms.environmentalControls: Sediment and erosion controls installed prior to earthworks. Concrete washout area designated. Hazardous materials stored in bunded area. Dust suppression by water cart as required. No burning of waste on site.
swms.signOffRequirements: Site supervisor sign-off required before work commences each day. All workers to sign attendance register. SWMS to be reviewed and re-signed if scope of work changes.

swms.title: Working at Heights
swms.workActivity: Any work performed at a height of 2 metres or more above the ground or a floor level, including roof work, scaffold erection, use of ladders, and elevated work platforms.
swms.hazards: Falls from height; falling tools and materials; unstable working surfaces; inadequate edge protection; ladder instability; EWP tip-over; adverse weather conditions.
swms.risks: Fatal or serious injury from falls; struck by falling objects; EWP rollover; electrocution from overhead power lines.
swms.controls: Eliminate the need to work at heights where possible through design. Use scaffolding with full edge protection (toe boards, mid-rails, top rails) as the preferred method. EWP to be used where scaffold is not practicable. Ladders only for access/egress, not as a working platform. Establish exclusion zones below work area. Inspect all equipment before use. Check weather forecast — cease work in winds >40km/h. Overhead power line exclusion zone minimum 3m (6.4m for 11kV+).
swms.ppe: Hard hat; Safety harness (AS/NZS 1891.1) with double lanyard when working on roof or unprotected edges; Safety boots; High visibility vest; Safety glasses; Gloves.
swms.plantEquipment: Scaffolding (AS/NZS 4576); Elevated Work Platforms (EWP); Extension ladders (AS/NZS 1892); Safety harness and lanyards; Anchor points.
swms.trainingCompetency: Scaffold erectors must hold a scaffolding licence (basic, intermediate or advanced as required). EWP operators must hold a relevant high risk work licence (WP class). All workers working at heights must be trained in harness use and rescue procedures.
swms.emergencyControls: Rescue plan in place for suspended worker. First aid officer on site. Emergency services contact numbers posted. Rescue equipment (rope, harness) accessible at height work areas.
swms.environmentalControls: Secure all materials and tools at height to prevent them falling. Use tool lanyards. Debris netting where required. Cease work in lightning, high winds or heavy rain.
swms.signOffRequirements: Supervisor to inspect scaffold and edge protection before each shift. Workers to sign SWMS before commencing work at heights. Permit to work required for unprotected roof edges.

swms.title: Excavation and Trenching
swms.workActivity: Excavation and trenching operations including machine excavation, hand digging, installation of underground services, and backfilling.
swms.hazards: Trench collapse and engulfment; underground services (gas, electrical, water, telecommunications); falling into excavation; plant operating near excavation edge; flooding; toxic or oxygen-deficient atmosphere.
swms.risks: Fatal engulfment from trench collapse; electrocution from underground cables; gas explosion; drowning; crush injuries from plant.
swms.controls: Obtain Dial Before You Dig (DBYD) report before any excavation. Pothole to confirm service locations. Maintain minimum 600mm clearance from services. Shore, batter or bench all trenches deeper than 1.5m. Establish exclusion zones around excavation edges. No plant within 1m of trench edge without engineer approval. Inspect trench walls after rain or vibration. Atmospheric testing in confined trenches. Dewatering pump on standby.
swms.ppe: Hard hat; High visibility vest; Safety boots; Safety glasses; Gloves; Hearing protection when operating plant.
swms.plantEquipment: Excavators; Trench shoring systems; Dewatering pumps; Atmospheric gas monitors; Dial Before You Dig service locator; Hand tools.
swms.trainingCompetency: Excavator operators must hold a relevant high risk work licence. Supervisor must be competent in trench safety assessment. Workers must be trained in confined space entry if applicable.
swms.emergencyControls: Rescue plan for trench collapse — do not enter collapsed trench. Call 000 immediately. Trench rescue equipment (rope, board) on site. First aid officer on site.
swms.environmentalControls: Sediment controls at trench entry/exit points. Spoil stored minimum 600mm from trench edge. Dewatering discharge to sediment basin. Protect tree root zones from excavation.
swms.signOffRequirements: Supervisor to inspect trench before workers enter each shift. DBYD report to be on site. Workers to sign SWMS before commencing excavation.

swms.title: Concrete Placement and Finishing
swms.workActivity: Receiving, placing, vibrating, screeding, and finishing concrete including slab-on-ground, footings, columns, and elevated slabs. Includes use of concrete pump and agitator trucks.
swms.hazards: Concrete burns (alkaline burns to skin and eyes); manual handling of heavy loads; concrete pump hose whip; agitator truck movement; vibration from power tools; slippery surfaces; working in formwork.
swms.risks: Chemical burns from wet concrete; musculoskeletal injuries; struck by pump hose; crush injuries from agitator truck; hand-arm vibration syndrome; falls on wet surfaces.
swms.controls: Wear full PPE including waterproof gloves and rubber boots when handling wet concrete. Wash skin immediately if contact occurs. Establish truck exclusion zone — spotter required for reversing. Concrete pump operator to hold relevant licence. Inspect pump hoses and couplings before use. Ensure formwork is inspected and certified before pour. Provide non-slip surfaces in work area. Rotate workers on vibrating equipment to limit exposure.
swms.ppe: Hard hat; High visibility vest; Rubber boots (knee-high); Waterproof gloves; Safety glasses or face shield; Hearing protection when using vibrators.
swms.plantEquipment: Concrete agitator trucks; Concrete pump; Internal vibrators; Screed rails; Power floats; Hand tools (rakes, trowels, floats).
swms.trainingCompetency: Concrete pump operator must hold a relevant high risk work licence. Formwork must be designed and certified by a structural engineer for elevated slabs. Workers trained in concrete burn first aid.
swms.emergencyControls: Eyewash station on site. First aid kit with burn treatment supplies. Nearest hospital confirmed. Formwork collapse rescue plan in place.
swms.environmentalControls: Concrete washout area designated and bunded. No concrete to enter stormwater drains. Excess concrete to be returned to plant or disposed of in designated washout area.
swms.signOffRequirements: Formwork inspection sign-off before pour commences. Supervisor to confirm pump setup and exclusion zones. Workers to sign SWMS before pour.

swms.title: Demolition — Minor Works
swms.workActivity: Minor demolition including removal of non-structural walls, ceilings, flooring, fixtures, and fittings. Excludes structural demolition which requires a separate SWMS.
swms.hazards: Asbestos-containing materials (ACM); lead paint; structural instability; falling debris; dust inhalation; manual handling; electrical hazards; noise.
swms.risks: Asbestos-related disease; lead poisoning; structural collapse; injury from falling debris; respiratory illness; musculoskeletal injuries; electrocution.
swms.controls: Conduct asbestos survey before any demolition. If ACM identified, engage licensed asbestos removalist. Isolate and lock out all electrical circuits in work area. Assess structural stability before removing any element. Wet down surfaces to suppress dust. Establish exclusion zone around demolition area. Segregate and label all waste. Lead paint — use wet methods and P2 respirator.
swms.ppe: Hard hat; High visibility vest; Safety boots; Safety glasses; P2 respirator (minimum) for dust; Disposable coveralls for asbestos/lead work; Gloves; Hearing protection.
swms.plantEquipment: Angle grinders; Reciprocating saws; Jackhammers; Pry bars; Dust extraction units; Skip bins.
swms.trainingCompetency: Asbestos awareness training for all workers. Licensed asbestos removalist for any friable or bonded ACM removal. Supervisor to hold demolition competency.
swms.emergencyControls: If unexpected ACM discovered — stop work, isolate area, notify supervisor. Do not disturb. Engage licensed assessor. First aid kit on site.
swms.environmentalControls: Asbestos waste to be double-bagged, labelled and disposed of at licensed facility. Lead paint waste segregated. Dust suppression throughout. No burning of demolition waste.
swms.signOffRequirements: Asbestos survey report on site before work commences. Electrical isolation certificate on site. Workers to sign SWMS. Supervisor sign-off each day.

swms.title: Electrical Work — General
swms.workActivity: Electrical installation, maintenance, testing, and inspection work including switchboard work, cable installation, fitting of outlets and fixtures, and testing and tagging.
swms.hazards: Electric shock and electrocution; arc flash; fire from electrical fault; working in confined spaces; falls from ladders; manual handling.
swms.risks: Fatal electrocution; severe burns from arc flash; fire; musculoskeletal injuries.
swms.controls: All electrical work to be performed by a licensed electrician. Isolate and lock out circuits before commencing work — use LOTO procedure. Test for dead before touching any conductor. Use insulated tools rated for the voltage. Wear arc flash PPE for switchboard work. Never work on live circuits unless absolutely necessary and with a permit to work. Inspect all tools and leads before use — test and tag current.
swms.ppe: Hard hat (non-conductive); Safety boots (non-conductive sole); Insulated gloves rated for voltage; Arc flash face shield and flame-resistant clothing for switchboard work; Safety glasses.
swms.plantEquipment: Multimeter; Insulated tools; LOTO devices; Test and tag equipment; Cable pulling equipment; Conduit bender.
swms.trainingCompetency: All electrical work must be performed by a licensed electrician (A-grade or restricted as applicable). Workers must be trained in LOTO procedures. First aid officer with CPR/AED training on site.
swms.emergencyControls: Do not touch a person in contact with live electricity. Isolate power first. Call 000. CPR-trained first aider on site. AED location communicated at induction.
swms.environmentalControls: Dispose of electrical waste (cables, fittings) in accordance with local regulations. No burning of cable insulation.
swms.signOffRequirements: Electrical isolation certificate before work on any circuit. Supervisor sign-off on LOTO procedure. Compliance certificate on completion.

swms.title: Plumbing and Drainage
swms.workActivity: Installation, maintenance, and repair of plumbing systems including water supply, drainage, hot water systems, gas fitting, and stormwater.
swms.hazards: Excavation hazards for underground work; hot water burns; gas leaks; confined space entry; manual handling; working at heights for roof drainage; chemical exposure from solvents and flux.
swms.risks: Burns from hot water/steam; gas explosion; engulfment in excavation; musculoskeletal injuries; chemical burns; falls.
swms.controls: Isolate water supply before commencing work on pressurised systems. Purge and test gas lines before and after work. Obtain gas work permit. Excavation SWMS to apply for underground work. Use appropriate PPE when handling chemicals. Ensure hot water systems are set to correct temperature (60°C storage, 50°C delivery to prevent scalding). Confined space entry procedure for work in pits.
swms.ppe: Hard hat; High visibility vest; Safety boots; Safety glasses; Chemical-resistant gloves for solvent/flux work; Hearing protection when using power tools.
swms.plantEquipment: Pipe cutters; Soldering equipment; Pipe threading machine; Drain camera; Pressure testing equipment; Excavation equipment (refer to Excavation SWMS).
swms.trainingCompetency: All plumbing and gas work must be performed by a licensed plumber/gasfitter. Workers must be trained in confined space entry if applicable.
swms.emergencyControls: Gas leak — evacuate area, call gas supplier emergency line and 000. Do not use electrical switches. Water leak — isolate supply. Burns — cool with running water for 20 minutes.
swms.environmentalControls: Prevent solvent and chemical spills entering stormwater. Dispose of chemical waste correctly. Protect waterways from sediment during excavation.
swms.signOffRequirements: Compliance certificate on completion of all licensed work. Pressure test results recorded. Workers to sign SWMS.

swms.title: Roofing — Metal and Tile
swms.workActivity: Installation, repair, and maintenance of metal roofing (Colorbond, corrugated iron, standing seam) and tile roofing (concrete and terracotta tiles). Includes guttering and downpipe installation.
swms.hazards: Falls from roof edge; falls through fragile roof surfaces (skylights, fibro, corroded sheeting); sharp metal edges; manual handling of heavy tiles; UV radiation; heat stress; adverse weather; overhead power lines.
swms.risks: Fatal or serious injury from falls; lacerations from metal edges; musculoskeletal injuries; heat exhaustion; electrocution from power lines.
swms.controls: Establish edge protection (scaffolding, safety mesh, or catch platform) before commencing roof work. Never walk on fibro/asbestos cement sheeting or fragile skylights — use roof ladders or crawl boards. Identify and maintain exclusion zone from overhead power lines (minimum 3m). Work in cooler parts of the day in summer. Wear cut-resistant gloves when handling metal sheeting. Secure all materials and tools on roof. Cease work in winds >40km/h or lightning.
swms.ppe: Hard hat; Safety harness with double lanyard anchored to certified anchor points; Safety boots with non-slip soles; Cut-resistant gloves; Safety glasses; High visibility vest; Sun protection.
swms.plantEquipment: Scaffolding; Roof ladders and crawl boards; Safety harness and anchor points; Tin snips; Nibblers; Screw guns; Tile cutters.
swms.trainingCompetency: Roofing workers must be trained in working at heights and harness use. Scaffold must be erected by licensed scaffolder. Asbestos awareness training required.
swms.emergencyControls: Rescue plan for suspended worker. First aid officer on site. Emergency contacts posted. Cease work and evacuate in lightning.
swms.environmentalControls: Secure all materials to prevent wind-blown debris. Collect and dispose of metal offcuts. Protect gutters from debris during installation.
swms.signOffRequirements: Scaffold inspection certificate before work commences. Anchor point certification on site. Workers to sign SWMS. Supervisor daily sign-off.

swms.title: Crane and Rigging Operations
swms.workActivity: Crane lifts including mobile crane, tower crane, and franna crane operations. Rigging of loads including structural steel, precast panels, plant and equipment.
swms.hazards: Load drop or swing; crane tip-over; rigging failure; workers in the drop zone; overhead power lines; ground instability under crane; communication failure.
swms.risks: Fatal crush injury from dropped or swinging load; crane collapse; electrocution from power lines; structural damage.
swms.controls: Lift study/plan required for all lifts. Crane to be set up on firm, level ground — engineer certification for soft ground. Establish exclusion zone equal to load radius plus 20%. Dogman to direct all lifts — no lift without dogman in visual contact. All rigging equipment to be inspected and rated for the load. Overhead power line exclusion zone — minimum 3m (contact supply authority for higher voltages). Two-way radio communication between crane operator and dogman. No personnel under suspended load.
swms.ppe: Hard hat; High visibility vest; Safety boots; Gloves; Safety glasses.
swms.plantEquipment: Mobile crane; Tower crane; Franna crane; Slings (chain, wire rope, webbing); Shackles; Spreader beams; Lifting lugs.
swms.trainingCompetency: Crane operator must hold a relevant high risk work licence (C2, C6 etc.). Dogman must hold a dogging licence (DG). Rigger must hold a rigging licence (RB, RI, RA as required). Lift study to be prepared by competent person.
swms.emergencyControls: If load drops — evacuate exclusion zone immediately. Call 000 if injury. Do not approach unstable crane. Incident notification to regulator required for dangerous incidents.
swms.environmentalControls: Hydraulic fluid spill kit on crane. Protect ground surface from crane outrigger loads. Noise management for residential areas.
swms.signOffRequirements: Lift study signed off by supervisor before lift. Rigging equipment inspection records on site. Workers to sign SWMS. Crane operator pre-start checklist completed.

swms.title: Confined Space Entry
swms.workActivity: Entry into confined spaces including pits, tanks, vaults, manholes, tunnels, and enclosed areas with restricted entry/exit and potential for hazardous atmosphere.
swms.hazards: Oxygen deficiency or enrichment; toxic gases (H2S, CO, methane); flammable atmosphere; engulfment; restricted entry/exit for rescue; heat stress; noise.
swms.risks: Asphyxiation; explosion; toxic gas poisoning; entrapment; heat exhaustion.
swms.controls: Confined space entry permit required before entry. Atmospheric testing (O2, CO, H2S, LEL) before and continuously during entry. Ventilate space before and during entry. Standby person at entry point at all times — never enters space. Rescue plan and equipment in place before entry. Isolate all energy sources (LOTO). Communicate with entrant at regular intervals. Entrant to wear harness for retrieval.
swms.ppe: Hard hat; Safety harness with retrieval line; SCBA or airline breathing apparatus if atmosphere cannot be made safe; Safety boots; Gloves; Intrinsically safe lighting and equipment.
swms.plantEquipment: Atmospheric gas monitor (4-gas); Forced ventilation fan; Tripod and winch for retrieval; SCBA; Intrinsically safe lighting; LOTO devices.
swms.trainingCompetency: Entry supervisor must hold confined space entry supervisor competency. Entrants and standby person must hold confined space training. Rescue team trained and equipped.
swms.emergencyControls: Do not enter to rescue without SCBA and trained rescue team. Retrieve entrant using tripod/winch if possible. Call 000. Rescue plan posted at entry point.
swms.environmentalControls: Prevent contaminants from entering confined space during work. Dispose of any materials removed from space correctly.
swms.signOffRequirements: Confined space entry permit signed by supervisor before each entry. Atmospheric test results recorded. Rescue plan signed off. Workers to sign SWMS.

swms.title: Hot Works — Welding, Cutting and Grinding
swms.workActivity: Hot works including arc welding, oxy-acetylene cutting, plasma cutting, angle grinding, and any work that produces sparks, heat, or open flame.
swms.hazards: Fire and explosion; UV radiation from welding arc; fumes and gases; burns; electric shock (arc welding); compressed gas cylinder hazards; noise; eye injury from grinding sparks.
swms.risks: Fire; explosion of flammable materials; arc eye; respiratory illness from fumes; burns; electrocution; hearing damage.
swms.controls: Hot work permit required in all areas except designated welding bays. Clear combustible materials minimum 10m from hot work area. Fire watch for minimum 30 minutes after hot work ceases. Inspect area for smouldering materials. Ensure adequate ventilation — use LEV for welding fumes. Inspect welding leads and equipment before use. Secure gas cylinders upright. Flashback arrestors on oxy-acetylene equipment. Grinding disc rated for tool RPM.
swms.ppe: Welding helmet with correct shade lens; Leather welding gloves; Leather apron or welding jacket; Safety boots; Hearing protection; P2 respirator for welding fumes; Safety glasses under welding helmet.
swms.plantEquipment: Welding machine; Oxy-acetylene set with flashback arrestors; Plasma cutter; Angle grinder; Fire extinguisher (CO2 or dry powder); Fire blanket.
swms.trainingCompetency: Welders must hold relevant trade qualification or demonstrated competency. Hot work permit issuer must be trained. Fire warden designated.
swms.emergencyControls: Fire extinguisher and fire blanket at hot work location. Fire warden on site. Evacuation plan posted. Call 000 for fire. Burns — cool with running water 20 minutes.
swms.environmentalControls: Collect grinding sparks and metal offcuts. Dispose of electrode stubs correctly. Prevent welding spatter from igniting vegetation.
swms.signOffRequirements: Hot work permit signed before work commences. Fire watch log maintained. Workers to sign SWMS. Supervisor sign-off.

swms.title: Concreting — Slab on Ground
swms.workActivity: Preparation and pouring of concrete slabs on ground including subgrade preparation, formwork erection, reinforcement placement, concrete delivery and placement, vibrating, screeding, and power floating to achieve a finished slab surface.
swms.hazards: Concrete burns (alkaline burns to skin and eyes from wet concrete); manual handling of reinforcement mesh and bar (sharp edges, heavy loads); agitator truck and concrete pump movement on site; concrete pump hose whip under pressure; vibrating equipment (hand-arm vibration); slippery wet concrete surfaces; working in formwork; UV radiation and heat stress during summer pours; noise from power floats and vibrators.
swms.risks: Chemical burns to skin and eyes from prolonged wet concrete contact; lacerations and musculoskeletal injuries from handling rebar and mesh; crush injuries from reversing agitator trucks; pump hose failure causing serious injury; hand-arm vibration syndrome from prolonged vibrator use; slips and falls on wet slab surface; heat exhaustion.
swms.controls: Wear full PPE including waterproof gloves and rubber boots at all times when handling wet concrete — wash any skin contact immediately with clean water. Establish truck exclusion zone with a dedicated spotter for all reversing agitator trucks. Concrete pump operator must hold a relevant high risk work licence; inspect all pump hoses, couplings and clamps before each pour. Formwork to be inspected and certified by supervisor before pour commences. Rotate workers on internal vibrators — maximum 10 minutes continuous use per operator. Provide non-slip duckboards across wet slab surface for access. Schedule pours in cooler parts of the day during summer; provide shade, cool water and rest breaks. Hearing protection mandatory when power floats are in use.
swms.ppe: Hard hat; High visibility vest; Rubber boots (knee-high, AS/NZS 2210); Waterproof nitrile or rubber gloves; Safety glasses or face shield during pump operation; Hearing protection when power floats or vibrators are in use; Sunscreen SPF50+ and sun-protective clothing for outdoor pours.
swms.plantEquipment: Concrete agitator trucks; Concrete pump (line or boom); Internal concrete vibrators; Screed rails and straight edge; Power float (helicopter); Hand tools (rakes, trowels, bull floats, edging tools); Formwork (timber or steel); Reinforcement bar and mesh; Bar chairs and spacers.
swms.trainingCompetency: Concrete pump operator must hold a relevant high risk work licence (CV class). Formwork for elevated slabs must be designed and certified by a structural engineer. All workers to be trained in concrete burn first aid. Supervisor to hold a current White Card and relevant trade experience.
swms.emergencyControls: Eyewash station positioned at pour location before work commences. First aid kit with burn treatment supplies on site. Nearest hospital and emergency contacts confirmed at site induction. In the event of formwork distress or collapse — evacuate all workers from the affected area immediately and call 000.
swms.environmentalControls: Designated concrete washout area established and bunded before pour commences — no concrete washout to enter stormwater drains or waterways. Excess concrete to be returned to batch plant or disposed of in the washout area. Pump washout water to be contained and allowed to set before disposal. Protect adjacent vegetation and site drainage from concrete spill.
swms.signOffRequirements: Formwork inspection and sign-off by supervisor before pour commences. Pump setup and exclusion zones confirmed by supervisor. Concrete delivery dockets retained on site. Workers to sign SWMS before pour. Supervisor daily sign-off.

swms.title: Demolition — Structural and Non-Structural
swms.workActivity: Demolition of structures including removal of non-structural walls, ceilings, flooring, fixtures and fittings, as well as partial structural demolition of load-bearing elements under engineering supervision. Includes manual demolition, mechanical demolition, and strip-out works.
swms.hazards: Asbestos-containing materials (ACM) in pre-1990 buildings; lead paint on surfaces; structural instability and unplanned collapse during demolition sequence; falling debris and materials; dust inhalation (silica, asbestos, general construction dust); manual handling of heavy debris; electrical hazards from live circuits; noise from jackhammers and power tools; working at heights during upper-level strip-out.
swms.risks: Fatal asbestos-related disease from fibre inhalation; lead poisoning from disturbing lead paint; structural collapse causing fatal crush injuries; respiratory illness from silica and dust exposure; electrocution from undiscovered live circuits; musculoskeletal injuries; hearing damage.
swms.controls: Obtain an asbestos survey and hazardous materials report before any demolition commences — engage a licensed asbestos assessor. If ACM is identified, engage a licensed asbestos removalist before demolition proceeds. Isolate and lock out (LOTO) all electrical circuits in the work area — obtain electrical isolation certificate. Engage a structural engineer to prepare a demolition sequence plan for any structural element removal; follow the sequence strictly. Establish a full exclusion zone around the demolition area — no unauthorised entry. Wet down surfaces to suppress dust before breaking. Use dust extraction on all power tools where practicable. Segregate and label all waste streams. For lead paint — use wet methods and P2 respirator minimum. Cease work and reassess if unexpected structural movement or cracking is observed.
swms.ppe: Hard hat; High visibility vest; Safety boots with steel cap and midsole; Safety glasses; P2 respirator for dust (minimum) — P3 full-face for asbestos or lead paint work; Disposable coveralls (Tyvek) for asbestos and lead paint work; Gloves (cut-resistant for sharp debris); Hearing protection when using jackhammers or power tools.
swms.plantEquipment: Excavator with demolition attachment (for mechanical demolition); Jackhammers; Angle grinders; Reciprocating saws; Pry bars and wrecking bars; Dust extraction units; Skip bins and waste containers; Asbestos waste bags (double-bag, labelled); LOTO devices.
swms.trainingCompetency: All workers must hold a current White Card and have completed asbestos awareness training. Licensed asbestos removalist required for any friable ACM or bonded ACM >10m2. Supervisor to hold a demolition competency or relevant trade licence. Structural demolition sequence to be prepared and signed off by a structural engineer.
swms.emergencyControls: If unexpected ACM is disturbed — stop work immediately, isolate the area, do not re-enter without a P2 respirator, notify supervisor and the WHS regulator if required. In the event of structural collapse — evacuate all workers, call 000, do not re-enter. First aid kit on site. Emergency contacts posted at site entry.
swms.environmentalControls: Asbestos waste to be double-bagged in labelled asbestos waste bags and disposed of at a licensed facility — retain disposal receipts. Lead paint waste segregated and disposed of as hazardous waste. Dust suppression throughout works. No burning of demolition waste on site. Protect stormwater drains from debris and dust runoff.
swms.signOffRequirements: Asbestos survey report and hazardous materials register on site before work commences. Electrical isolation certificate on site. Structural demolition sequence plan signed off by engineer. Workers to sign SWMS before commencing. Supervisor sign-off each day.

swms.title: Elevated Work Platform (EWP) Operations
swms.workActivity: Operation of elevated work platforms including boom-type EWPs (knuckle boom, straight boom), scissor lifts, and vertical personnel lifts for work at height including installation, maintenance, inspection, and construction tasks.
swms.hazards: Falls from the EWP platform; EWP tip-over on uneven or soft ground; overhead power lines and overhead obstructions; entrapment of operator between platform and fixed structure; falling tools and materials from platform; EWP mechanical failure; ground personnel struck by moving EWP; working in adverse weather (wind, lightning).
swms.risks: Fatal or serious injury from falls from height; EWP rollover causing crush injury; electrocution from contact with overhead power lines; entrapment causing serious injury; struck-by injury to ground personnel; equipment damage from collision.
swms.controls: Only operators holding a relevant high risk work licence (WP class — boom-type EWP >11m) may operate boom EWPs. Conduct a pre-start inspection of the EWP before each use — check tyres, controls, safety devices, harness anchor points, and fuel/charge level. Assess ground conditions before positioning — use outrigger pads on soft or uneven ground; obtain engineer approval for suspended floors. Identify all overhead power lines and obstructions before commencing — maintain minimum 3m exclusion zone from power lines (contact supply authority for higher voltages). Operator must wear a full-body harness connected to the anchor point inside the platform at all times when elevated. Establish a ground exclusion zone around the EWP travel path and working radius. Cease operations in winds exceeding 45km/h or in lightning. Never exceed the rated platform capacity.
swms.ppe: Hard hat; Full-body safety harness (AS/NZS 1891.1) connected to EWP anchor point; Safety boots with non-slip soles; High visibility vest; Safety glasses; Gloves; Hearing protection if using power tools on platform.
swms.plantEquipment: Boom-type EWP (knuckle boom, straight boom); Scissor lift; Vertical personnel lift; Full-body harness and lanyard; Outrigger pads; Pre-start inspection checklist.
swms.trainingCompetency: Boom-type EWP operators (>11m) must hold a high risk work licence (WP class). Scissor lift and EWP <11m operators must hold documented competency (operator training certificate). All operators to complete a site-specific familiarisation before use. Rescue plan for a stranded or incapacitated operator must be in place before work commences.
swms.emergencyControls: Rescue plan for stranded or incapacitated operator to be documented and communicated before work commences — include manual lowering procedure. If EWP contacts power line — operator to stay in platform and call for help; do not attempt to exit until power is confirmed isolated. Call 000 for any injury. First aid officer on site.
swms.environmentalControls: Prevent hydraulic fluid leaks — inspect EWP before use and report any leaks. Use drip trays under EWP when operating over sensitive areas. Avoid operating on soft ground that may cause rutting or damage to landscaping.
swms.signOffRequirements: Pre-start inspection checklist completed and signed before each use. Operator licence or competency certificate sighted by supervisor. Ground conditions and overhead hazard assessment documented. Workers to sign SWMS before commencing. Supervisor sign-off.

swms.title: Landscaping and Grounds Maintenance
swms.workActivity: Landscaping and grounds maintenance activities including mowing, line trimming, hedge trimming, pruning, mulching, planting, irrigation installation, retaining wall construction, turf laying, and general grounds upkeep on residential and commercial sites.
swms.hazards: Projectile objects from mowers and line trimmers (rocks, debris); contact with rotating blades; manual handling of heavy materials (soil, turf rolls, retaining wall blocks, pots); working near traffic and pedestrians; chemical exposure from herbicides, pesticides, and fertilisers; UV radiation and heat stress; insect and snake bites; working near underground services; noise from power equipment; dust from dry soil and mulch.
swms.risks: Eye and body injury from projectile debris; lacerations from blade contact; musculoskeletal injuries from manual handling; struck by vehicle; chemical poisoning or skin/eye irritation; heat exhaustion; anaphylaxis from insect sting; electrocution or gas explosion from underground service strike; hearing damage; respiratory illness from dust.
swms.controls: Inspect work area before commencing — remove rocks, wire, and debris from mowing areas. Establish exclusion zones around mowing and trimming operations — minimum 15m for mowers, 5m for line trimmers. Wear full PPE including face shield when operating mowers and trimmers. Obtain DBYD report before any excavation or post-hole drilling. Manual handling — use mechanical aids (wheelbarrow, trolley, mini loader) for heavy loads; team lift for loads >20kg. Apply herbicides and pesticides strictly in accordance with the product label and SDS — do not apply in wind >15km/h. Implement sun and heat management plan — schedule heavy work in cooler parts of the day, provide shade and cool water. Conduct a snake awareness briefing at site induction. Rotate workers on noisy equipment to limit exposure.
swms.ppe: Hard hat or broad-brim sun hat; High visibility vest; Safety boots with steel cap; Full-face shield or safety glasses and face guard when operating mowers/trimmers; Hearing protection when operating power equipment; Chemical-resistant gloves and apron when handling herbicides/pesticides; P2 respirator for dusty conditions; Sunscreen SPF50+ and sun-protective clothing.
swms.plantEquipment: Ride-on mowers; Push mowers; Line trimmers; Hedge trimmers; Chainsaws (refer to separate SWMS); Chippers/mulchers; Mini excavators and skid steers; Plate compactors; Hand tools (shovels, rakes, mattocks); Irrigation installation tools.
swms.trainingCompetency: Chainsaw operators must hold a relevant chainsaw competency certificate. Chemical applicators must hold a current ChemCert or equivalent chemical handling certificate. Plant operators (mini excavator, skid steer) must hold relevant high risk work licences. All workers to hold a current White Card for construction sites.
swms.emergencyControls: First aid kit on site or in work vehicle at all times. In the event of a chemical splash to eyes — flush with clean water for 15 minutes and seek medical attention; have SDS available for emergency services. Snake bite — keep patient calm and still, apply pressure immobilisation bandage, call 000. Blade contact — apply direct pressure, call 000. Emergency contacts posted in work vehicle.
swms.environmentalControls: Mix and apply chemicals strictly per label — do not apply near waterways, stormwater drains, or in wind. Contain and dispose of chemical containers at an approved facility. Prevent soil and mulch from entering stormwater drains. Protect existing vegetation from damage during earthworks. Dispose of green waste at an approved facility or compost on site.
swms.signOffRequirements: Site hazard assessment completed before commencing each day. Chemical application records maintained (product, rate, area, date, operator). Workers to sign SWMS before commencing. Supervisor sign-off.

swms.title: Painting — Internal and External
swms.workActivity: Internal and external painting works including surface preparation (sanding, scraping, filling, priming), application of paints and coatings by brush, roller, and spray, and associated tasks such as masking, drop sheeting, and clean-up. Includes work at heights using ladders, scaffolding, and EWPs.
swms.hazards: Falls from ladders, scaffolding, and EWPs; chemical exposure from paints, solvents, thinners, and strippers (VOCs, isocyanates in two-pack coatings); lead paint in pre-1990 buildings; dust from sanding and surface preparation (silica dust); fire and explosion from flammable solvents; manual handling; UV radiation and heat stress for external work; spray painting overspray and mist inhalation.
swms.risks: Fatal or serious injury from falls; respiratory illness and chemical sensitisation from solvent and isocyanate exposure; lead poisoning from sanding lead paint; silicosis from silica dust; fire or explosion from flammable solvents; musculoskeletal injuries; heat exhaustion; eye and skin irritation.
swms.controls: Establish edge protection (scaffolding or EWP) for all work above 2m — ladders only for access, not as a working platform for extended tasks. Inspect all ladders and scaffolding before use. Ensure adequate ventilation in all internal painting areas — open windows and doors, use forced ventilation fans; never use solvent-based products in confined spaces without supplied air. Read SDS for all products before use — wear appropriate respiratory protection (P2 for dust and water-based products; organic vapour cartridge respirator for solvent-based products; full-face supplied air for two-pack isocyanate coatings). Test for lead paint in pre-1990 buildings before sanding or stripping — use wet methods and P2 respirator if lead paint is present. Eliminate ignition sources when using flammable solvents — no smoking, no open flames, use intrinsically safe equipment. Store flammable materials in a bunded, ventilated flammables cabinet. Rotate workers on sanding tasks to limit silica dust exposure.
swms.ppe: Hard hat when working at heights; Safety harness when working on unprotected edges; Safety boots; Safety glasses or goggles; Respiratory protection (P2 dust mask for sanding; organic vapour respirator for solvent-based paints; supplied air for two-pack coatings); Chemical-resistant gloves; Disposable coveralls for spray painting and lead paint work; High visibility vest on external sites.
swms.plantEquipment: Scaffolding; Extension ladders; EWP; Airless spray equipment; Conventional spray guns; Sanders (orbital, belt, pole); Scrapers and filling knives; Mixing equipment; Drop sheets and masking materials; Flammables storage cabinet; Forced ventilation fans.
swms.trainingCompetency: All painters to hold a Certificate III in Painting and Decorating or demonstrated trade competency. Workers using two-pack isocyanate coatings must hold specific training in isocyanate hazards and supplied air equipment. Lead paint awareness training for all workers on pre-1990 buildings. Working at heights training and harness use for all elevated work.
swms.emergencyControls: Fire extinguisher (CO2 or dry powder) in all areas where flammable solvents are in use. In the event of solvent fire — evacuate, call 000, do not use water on solvent fire. Chemical splash to eyes — flush with clean water for 15 minutes, seek medical attention, have SDS available. Solvent inhalation — move to fresh air, call 000 if symptoms persist. First aid kit on site.
swms.environmentalControls: Contain all paint and solvent waste — do not allow to enter stormwater drains or waterways. Dispose of paint tins, solvent containers, and contaminated rags at an approved facility. Use drop sheets to protect surfaces and collect overspray. Water-based paint washout water to be contained and disposed of correctly — not to stormwater. Minimise spray painting in windy conditions to prevent overspray drift.
swms.signOffRequirements: SDS for all products to be on site before work commences. Lead paint test results documented if applicable. Scaffold inspection certificate before elevated work. Workers to sign SWMS before commencing. Supervisor sign-off each day.

swms.title: Asbestos Awareness — Incidental Disturbance
swms.workActivity: Work activities where asbestos-containing materials (ACM) may be incidentally disturbed, including drilling, cutting, or removing materials in buildings constructed before 1990.
swms.hazards: Inhalation of asbestos fibres causing mesothelioma, lung cancer, and asbestosis; unexpected discovery of ACM during renovation or demolition.
swms.risks: Fatal asbestos-related disease from fibre inhalation.
swms.controls: Assume all materials in pre-1990 buildings may contain asbestos until proven otherwise. Obtain asbestos register or survey before commencing work. If ACM identified — stop work, do not disturb, notify supervisor. Engage licensed asbestos assessor to test and identify. Licensed asbestos removalist for removal of >10m2 non-friable or any friable ACM. Wet methods to suppress dust if minor disturbance unavoidable. Decontamination procedure on exit from work area.
swms.ppe: P2 respirator (minimum) — full-face respirator with P3 filter for higher risk; Disposable coveralls (Tyvek); Rubber gloves; Safety boots (cleanable).
swms.plantEquipment: Asbestos identification test kits; Wet spray equipment; Asbestos waste bags (double-bag, labelled); Decontamination unit for licensed removal.
swms.trainingCompetency: All workers must complete asbestos awareness training. Asbestos removal supervisor must hold a supervisory certificate. Licensed removalist for removal work.
swms.emergencyControls: If unexpected ACM disturbed — stop work immediately. Isolate area. Do not re-enter without P2 respirator. Notify supervisor and WHS regulator if required.
swms.environmentalControls: Asbestos waste double-bagged in labelled asbestos waste bags. Disposed of at licensed facility. Decontaminate tools and equipment before removing from work area.
swms.signOffRequirements: Asbestos register/survey on site before work commences. Workers to sign SWMS confirming asbestos awareness training. Supervisor sign-off.
